summary:
## Operating a Handheld Sewing Machine

This guide covers the key steps to successfully set up and use a battery-powered handheld sewing machine.

### ## Machine Preparation
- **Safety Lock**: Always engage the safety lock when you are not actively sewing. This prevents the machine from starting accidentally.
- **Batteries**: The machine requires four **AA batteries**. Install them according to the polarity symbols inside the battery compartment.
- **Thread Spindle**: Place a small bobbin on the short pin with the spring, or use the included longer pin for larger spools of thread.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Always keep the machine in the **locked position** when threading, placing fabric, or when it's not in use to prevent injury.

### ## Threading the Machine
Correct threading is essential for the machine to function. Follow this path:
1.  From the bobbin, guide the thread up through the **first thread guide**.
2.  Pass the thread between the two **tension disks** on the side knob.
3.  Hook the thread over the small **hook** located under the machine's arm.
4.  Thread the needle from **back to front**.

> [!TIP]
> Use the included **needle threader** to easily pass the thread through the eye of the needle. It's much faster than doing it by hand.

### ## Sewing Techniques
- **Tabletop Method**: The easiest way to sew is to rest the machine on a table. Use one hand to operate the power button and the other to guide the fabric.
- **Mid-Fabric Start**: To hem pants or start away from an edge, lift the **fastening plate**, raise the needle using the **rotary wheel**, position your fabric, and then lower the plate to begin sewing.
- **Vertical Method**: You can also operate the machine while holding it vertically, though this can be more awkward.

### ## Finishing Your Seam

> [!IMPORTANT]
> These machines create a **chain stitch**, which will unravel easily if not properly secured.

To secure your stitch at the end of a seam:
1.  Let the machine run without fabric to create a long thread tail (around 8 inches / 20 cm).
2.  Snip the thread.
3.  Turn the fabric over to the backside.
4.  Locate the **last loop** of the stitch.
5.  Pull the thread tail (from the front side) **through this last loop** to the back. This provides a basic lock.

For a more secure finish, use the hook tool to create a knot by pulling the thread tail through the final stitch loop again.

## Introduction

Hi, Domenica here from easypsewingforbeginners.com. In this video today, I'll be showing you how to operate a handheld sewing machine. 

I'll be using the Handy Stitch brand, but they're all very similar. So hopefully this video can help you today, no matter which brand you have. 

Okay, so usually when you get your Handy Stitch out of the box, it will already be threaded up and have fabric in it. I've already taken the fabric out and I'm going to unthread it so I can show you step-by-step how to thread the machine up.

## Initial Setup: Safety & Batteries

Okay, so I'm going to remove this bobbin of thread. Okay. So what I'm going to do before I do anything else with this machine, I'm going to put it into the lock position. So you have the operating button at the top here and there's a little lock here. So most machines should have something like this. So to lock it, we just slide it in under that button. Okay.

Now this is a battery-operated machine. So I'm going to load the batteries into the bottom here. Now this takes four AA batteries and it's got some little symbols on the side to help you see which way they need to go. Okay, so my batteries are all loaded up, and I'll just check. Yes, those work. I'm just going to lock it again now. 

I always like to keep it in the lock position when I'm not operating it because you can accidentally press the button when you don't mean to. I've done it a few times. Okay, so just to be safe, keep it in the lock position when you're not actually sewing with it.

## Loading the Thread Bobbin

Okay. The next thing we need to do is we need to get some thread into it. Now you'd have this little pin that comes on the machine and you may also get a spare longer pin as well. So if you actually want to use a spool of thread like this, you can just use that instead of having the thread on the bobbin. Okay. I'm just going to use the short one for today.

So I've got a bobbin loaded up here with some pink thread to make it easy for you to see hopefully. So I'm going to put my pin through the bobbin of thread there and I've got my spring on there. Now this comes loose, so be careful not to drop it because it is hard to find on a floor. I'm gonna push that pin into that spot there. Okay, you know it doesn't really matter which way the thread is coming off the bobbin.

## Threading the Machine Path

The first thread guide is right here, so we need to pass the thread from the bottom through to the top. Okay, like so. Hopefully you can see that. 

Okay, and then the next thread guide is actually the tension disks here. So just on this little knob here, you have two little disks. Okay, the thread needs to sit in between those two little disks. Okay, and just hanging down like so. 

All right, now the next thread guide is a little bit of a tricky one. So right underneath the arm here, you can see a hook. Okay, and the thread needs to be hooked, needs to be over that hook. So, just going to use my fingers here, so bear with me. Okay. So hopefully you can see that, put the thread over the hook there.

## Threading the Needle

Okay, and the last thing we need to do is we need to put the thread through the needle, going from the back through to the front. Now the direction is quite important. Now, the easiest way I've found to do this is with the little needle threader that we've given you in the little pack. So I put the little hook through the hole or the eye of the needle and I have the hook facing down, and just need to hook the thread under that hook. It would be much easier if this was on the table, but I'm holding it here so it's easy for you guys to see. Okay, and just hold that thread out and carefully pull that hook through the eye of the needle. I've just got a little loop, I'll see if I can get that. I'm going to have to try that again. Okay, once you've got that little loop through, just pull the thread tail all the way through.

## Key Machine Components

Okay. Now the machine is threaded and ready to use. Before we do that, I'm just going to show a couple of other parts. Here we have the rotary wheel, so this allows you to take the needle up and down. So it doesn't matter which direction you use it in, either way works. Okay, and we also have this one, this bit here. This is the fastening plate. Okay, and I'll be showing you how to use that in a minute.

## How to Sew on a Table

All right. We're ready to sew so I'm going to show you the way that I prefer to use it or the easiest way that I think to use it. The easiest way I found is to have the little handheld sewing machine sitting on your table like so. I use my left finger to operate the on/off switch and then I use my right hand to guide the fabric through. Okay, so I've just got two pieces of cotton fabric here that I'm using. 

Alright, so the easiest way I've found, when you're ready, unlock the machine. Just place your fabric at the beginning of the fastening plate here. So the fabric is going to be pulled from this direction towards the back. Okay, or if you're holding it this way, it's going to go from right to left. Okay. All right so I've got it flat on the table. Right. I'm going to press the button down. 

Okay, so it's started sewing. Now if you've just threaded the machine up, what I suggest you do, because you're going to have that thread tail that's going to be getting in the way there, if you just grab that thread and just pull that all the way through. That will keep it out of the way of getting tangled up in your stitching there.

## Preventing the Chain Stitch from Unraveling

Okay, so I've reached the end of my fabric. So what I'm actually going to do, I'll just turn it around so you can see it a bit easier. I don't usually turn it around at this point, but when you get to the end of your stitching what you need to do is put your thumb and your finger on that last stitch like that and just let it sew, so the thread comes out maybe until you've got about 20 centimeters or 8 inches or so, and just snip it in between. 

Okay, now the reason why I suggest you hold the thread is because when you actually pull this, because it does a chain stitch, if you pull that thread now and just leave it as it is, your sewing is going to gradually come unstitched. Okay. So what you need to do at this point is you turn your fabric over and you need to find the last loop. Okay, and you need to pull that thread tail from the front through to the back. Okay, and that will help to stop your stitching from coming undone.

## Creating a Secure Knot

Now I'll just show you what else I suggest you do to stop it from unraveling or to make it a bit more secure. So to secure your thread even more, grab the little hook that came with your pack. And what I like to do is just create a little loop with this thread. So lay it down like so, okay, I'm going to keep my finger on that loop and at the same time, I'm going to pass this little hook, with the little hook bit facing down, under the last stitch. And we're gonna grab that thread and pull it under that stitch. Pull it all the way through, don't let that little loop come through. And then I'm just going to pass that thread tail through the loop and pull it nice and tight. And that will keep your thread even more secure. 

Okay now the other end should be fine. Okay, but if you want you can do the same thing with that end.

## Starting a Seam Mid-Fabric

Now the other way that you can start sewing with this, especially if you're hemming pants or the bottom of a t-shirt and you don't actually want to start sewing right from the edge is... I'm just going to make sure that's locked... you can actually lift up the fastening plate. Okay, so very carefully. Okay, without pushing down on this arm because sometimes when you push on the arm, it could make it feel like it's going to sew your finger. So lift up this fastening plate and make sure the needle is in the highest position by using that rotary wheel. And you can place your fabric under the needle where you want to start sewing. Okay, and the same thing, and unlock and sew.

## Vertical Sewing Technique

Now you can also use the handheld sewing machine holding it vertically to your body, if that makes sense. So with your fabric under the fastening plate, unlock and you can sew like so. I find that way a little bit more awkward, but try both ways and see what works best for you.

## Conclusion & Further Resources

Okay. I hope you've found this video useful. Hit the thumbs up if you have. Subscribe to keep up to date with any new videos. If you have any problems with this machine and you would like some help with troubleshooting, then pop a comment down below and I'll try my best to answer it for you.
